items: (added to (normally feminine) nouns, forms diminutives, sometimes with a further change in meaning) — жи́ла (“vein”) + -ка → жи́лка (“veinlet, small vein”); моги́ла (“grave”) + -ка → моги́лка (“small grave”); бума́га (“paper, document”) + -ка → бума́жка (“small document”)

(added to nouns denoting classes of people, forms the feminine equivalent; replaces the suffix -ец if present) — ленингра́дец (“resident of Leningrad”) + -ка → ленингра́дка (“female resident of Leningrad”)

(added to verbs, forms abstract nouns or nouns indicating the result of the action) — закали́ть (“to temper, to harden”) + -ка → зака́лка (“tempering, hardening; training (for endurance)”); мочи́ть (“to soak, to wet”) + -ка → мо́чка (“soaking, wetting”); отде́лать (“to finish, to trim”) + -ка → отде́лка (“finishing, trimming; finish, trim”)
(added to verbs, forms instruments or tools) — заколо́ть (“to attach with a pin”) + -ка → зако́лка (“barrette”); пили́ть (“to saw”) + -ка → пи́лка (“fretsaw; fingernail file”)

(added to adjectives or numerals, forms colloquial nouns with the meaning of a carrier of the adjective's or numeral's properties) — минера́льный (“mineral (relational)”) + -ка → минера́лка (“mineral water (colloquial); mineral fertilizer (colloquial)”); зени́тный (“zenith (relational); anti-aircraft (relational)”) + -ка → зени́тка (“anti-aircraft gun (colloquial)”); полтора́ (“one and a half”) + -ка → полу́торка (“small apartment consisting of a medium-sized room and a small room (colloquial); GAZ-AA-brand truck with a 1.5-ton payload (colloquial)”)

(highly productive suffix) takes masculine nouns, produces diminutive masculine nouns, sometimes with further sense development — дуб (“oak”) + -о́к → дубо́к (“oakling, little oak”); шум (“noise”) + -о́к → шумо́к (“noise”); чай (“tea”) + -ёк → чаёк (“tea”)

(highly productive suffix, takes given name, produces given name, diminutive) paired with -ик, -ук, -юк — И́горь (“Igor”) + -ёк → Игорёк (“little Igor”); Са́ша (“Sasha”) + -о́к → Сашо́к (“little Sasha”); Васили́са (“Vasilisa”) + -ёк → Василёк (“little Vasilisa”)

(productive suffix, colloquial, unstressed, takes verbs, produces nouns) an object that remains after process is done — обре́зать (“to clip, to trim”) + -ок → обре́зок (“clipping”); объесть (“to eat away”) + -ок → объе́док (“scrap”); о- + кури́ть (“to smoke”) + -ок → оку́рок (“butt”)
(animate, takes verbs, produces nouns) agent — е́здить (“to ride”) + -о́к → ездо́к (“rider”); стреля́ть (“to shoot”) + -о́к → стрело́к (“shooter”); знать (“to know”) + -о́к → знато́к (“cognoscente”)

(takes verbs, produces nouns) a tool or means of an action — скрести + -о́к → скребо́к (“scraper”); мани́ть (“to lure”) + -о́к → мано́к (“bait”); пома́зать (“to oil, to lubricate”) + -о́к → помазо́к (“shaving brush”)

(inanimate, takes verbs, produces nouns) subject of an action — расти́ (“to grow”) + -о́к → росто́к (“sprout, shoot”); гуде́ть (“to hoot, to honk”) + -о́к → гудо́к (“hooter, car honk”); по- + пла́вать (“to swim, to float”) + -о́к → поплаво́к (“float”)
(takes verbs, produces nouns) place of an action — ката́ться (“to ski, to skate”) + -о́к → като́к (“ice skating rink”)

(productive suffix, colloquial, stressed, takes verbs, produces nouns) one occurrence of an action; separate act — глота́ть (“to swallow”) + -о́к → глото́к (“swallow, gulp”); кива́ть (“to nod, to beckon”) + -о́к → киво́к (“nod”); зевать (“to yawn, to gape”) + -о́к → зево́к (“yawn, gape”)
(takes adjective, produces nouns) — жёлтый (“yellow”) + -о́к → желто́к (“yolk”); бе́лый (“white”) + -о́к → бело́к (“egg white; white (of the eye)”); бе́лый (“white”) + -ёк → белёк (“young seal”)
(with недо-, productive suffix, colloquial, takes nouns, produces nouns) undeveloped or transitional object
(takes nouns, produces nouns) paired with -иц, -ица, -ак, -ака, -як, -яка; a piece of, one of them
(with за-, unproductive suffix, takes nouns, produces nouns) an object behind something or in the background
(with за-, unproductive suffix, takes nouns, produces nouns) located behind and look alike
(with о-, unproductive suffix, takes nouns, produces nouns) adjacent
(with от-, unproductive suffix, takes nouns, produces nouns) separated from, produced by
(with па-, unproductive suffix, produces nouns) alike, but not equal
(with пере-, slightly productive suffix, produces nouns) paired with -и; in between, during break (about location or time)
(with пере-, unproductive suffix, produces nouns) paired with -и, -ица; crossing, intersection
(with под-, unproductive suffix, produces nouns) beneath
(with под-, unproductive suffix, produces nouns) paired with -ик, -ник; undeveloped animal or object
(with при-, unproductive suffix, produces nouns) paired with -ник, -ень; adjacent
(with при-, unproductive suffix, produces nouns) paired with -ка; adjacent
(with про-, unproductive suffix, produces nouns) in between
(unproductive suffix, produces nouns) overdone, with a negative outcome
(unproductive suffix, animate, or, inanimate, produces nouns) subject with a qualifier in the first stem

Suffix added to normally masculine nouns to form diminutives, sometimes with a further change in meaning. — за́яц (“hare”) + -ик → за́йчик (“little hare, bunny; darling, sweetheart; reflection of a light beam”)

Suffix added to normally masculine names to form diminutives, often shortening the name in the process. — Алекса́ндр (“Alexander”) + -ик → А́лик (“Alex”); Алексе́й (“Alexei”) + -ик → А́лик (“Alex”); Влади́мир (“Vladimir”) + -ик → Вла́дик (“Vlad”)
Suffix appended to words, especially adjectives, to create masculine agent nouns, usually denoting a profession, performer, place, object, tool or a feature: -er, -or, -ant, -ic, -ist

blocks.text: The diminutive suffix is always unstressed and normally does not trigger any change in the stress, although in some cases the stress is drawn onto the preceding syllable (e.g., воло́сик from во́лос).
The agent-noun suffix is often stressed.

When added onto a noun ending in ц, the suffix triggers the Slavic first palatalization, resulting in ч. The same would be expected to happen to the velars к, г and х, but there appear to be no examples of this.
